I added `GET /users/{id}` in `main.go`. It returns the user as JSON with a 200, or a 404 with `{"error":"user not found"}`. An id that isn't an integer (like `/users/abc`) also gets a 404. `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` both pass. I didn't start the server or request the endpoint, so the handler hasn't been run.

I used Context7 to confirm that `r.PathValue` is available in Go 1.22 and later. The handler reads the id with it and looks the user up in the existing map under the read lock.

The seeded store has one user, id 1 (Ada), so `/users/1` returns her.

I added `GET /users/{id}` in `main.go`. It returns the user as JSON with a 200, or a 404 with `{"error":"user not found"}`. An id that isn't an integer (like `/users/abc`) also gets a 404. `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` both pass. I didn't start the server or request the endpoint, so the handler hasn't been run.

I used Context7 to confirm that `r.PathValue` is available in Go 1.22 and later. The handler reads the id with it and looks the user up in the existing map under the read lock.

The seeded store has one user, id 1 (Ada), so `/users/1` returns her.
